correctness.rationale: Fix rank-m square-zero X on a 2m-space: image=kernel and there are [2m choose m]_q|GL_m(q)| such X. In adapted splitting, all commuting Y have block form [[A,B],[0,A]], and Y²=0 iff A²=0 and AB+BA=0. Then rank(XY)=rank(A)=r≤floor(m/2). A rank-r square-zero operator is counted by flags imA⊆kerA and an isomorphism, giving [m choose r]_q[m−r choose r]_q|GL_r|. For h=m−2r, the anti-commutation equation forces B=[[P,Q,R],[0,S,T],[0,0,−P]]. Rank Y=2r+rankS, so rankY=m iff S∈GL_h, with q^{2r(m−r)} free P,Q,R,T choices. Multiplication proves exact asserted product-rank stratum size for every prime power including even characteristic; each stratum attainable. Independent explicit enumerations for canonical m=2 over F2,F3 found Y counts (6,12) and (48,72) for r=0,1. These tests corroborate, not replace, the block count.

originality.rationale: Levy 2006/2007 studies the varieties of commuting square-zero matrices and their irreducible-component rank labels, chiefly algebraic-closure geometry; Britnell–Wildon study which similarity types/classes commute, while Basili–Iarrobino concern Jordan partitions/Hilbert functions. Those do not present the finite-field counts of LABELED maximal-rank pairs stratified by rank XY. Previously described mutual annihilation corresponds to r=0 only, not r>0. Novelty is best-of-knowledge against closely related module enumeration; a non-indexed rational-point formula remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite representation-theory exact point-count may already imply the formula
Statement is for labeled matrices, not conjugacy classes or arbitrary nilpotent pairs; finite checks limited to small fields

value.rationale: The locus of commuting square-zero matrices models modules over k[x,y]/(x²,y²) and is a standard representation-geometric object. Its product rank measures a genuine nonzero multiplication invariant. Exact finite-field labeled rational-point stratum counts and an attained rank cutoff r≤floor(m/2) furnish a natural complete distribution beyond the mutually annihilating boundary, usable in enumeration of restricted module varieties.
